description: Functions that agents can call. Your own tools are checked and run in a sandbox.
sandboxNote: Sandbox for testing and running your own tools: {{sandbox}} (can be changed in the settings).

trustNote.user-authored: Written by you: runs in a separate Python process without isolation on this computer.
trustNote.untrusted: AI-created or of unknown origin: runs only isolated, here in the Docker sandbox.
trustNote.untrustedBlocked: AI-created or of unknown origin: runs only isolated, but neither the built-in Linux sandbox nor Docker is available. Agents with this tool cannot run; see Settings → Sandbox.
trustNote.untrustedBuiltin: AI-created or of unknown origin: runs only isolated, here in the built-in Linux sandbox (no network, no access to your files or keys). This stays so after your approval.
trustNote.mcp: This tool belongs to the connected service {{server}} (there: {{name}}). A call sends its arguments to that service; the answer is foreign text, never an instruction.

delete: Delete tool: withdraws it; agents with this tool cannot start again until you remove it from them
tryHint: Calls the tool with this input, as an agent would.

write.intro: Write a Python function with types and a docstring. Name, description and input schema are derived from it. Tests are test_* functions that call the function. On saving, everything is checked statically and the tests run in the sandbox. Write code, names and docstrings in English: agents read them in every language.

generate.question: What should the tool be able to do?
generate.hint: A Coding Agent writes code and tests. Both are checked statically, the tests run in the sandbox. Then you decide whether the tool is added.
generate.placeholder: e.g. Calculate the annuity of a loan from amount, annual interest rate in percent and term in months.
generate.reviewNote: Review code and tests before approving the tool. Approved tools can be used by all agents.
generate.dependenciesNote: The proposal uses third-party libraries. Nothing is installed; the tests only run after your approval. You approve the code separately afterwards.
generate.needsDocker: Creating tools with AI needs isolation: the tests of AI-written code never run without it. The built-in Linux sandbox is not available here (see Settings → Sandbox); choose Docker instead.

drafts.label: Tool drafts
drafts.text: The Workflow Architect wrote these tools. They are not registered and have not run. Agents that need them cannot start until you approve them.

sandboxBuiltin: separate Python process; AI-created tools in the built-in Linux sandbox

services.title: Connected services
services.intro: Connect external services through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). An agent sees a tool only after you have reviewed and approved it.
services.emptyText: Connect an MCP server by its address. Then test the connection and approve its tools one by one.
services.counts: Tools approved: {{approved}} of {{total}} · waiting for review: {{pending}}
services.unavailable: MCP is not available in this installation (needs Python 3.11 or later). Services can be set up but not reached.
services.endpointList: The operator allows only these addresses: {{list}}
services.endpointListEmpty: The operator has not allowed any addresses for MCP (NODESTRO_MCP_ENDPOINTS). Services cannot be connected here.
services.noVault: No secure key store available: access tokens are not saved, only kept in memory until the app closes.
services.readOnlyMvp: For now only tools you classify as "read only" can be used.
services.writeEnabled: Tools that change data need an approval for each call.
services.unattendedOff: Schedules, batches and published APIs do not use service tools.
services.unattendedOn: The operator has enabled use in runs without a person.

accessHint.read: Read only: the tool changes nothing at the service or elsewhere. A reading tool still receives the arguments the agent sends.
accessHint.write: Changes data: creates, changes or sends something. When in doubt, this is the right classification.
accessHint.destructive: Deletes or destroys: can remove data for good.

services.changedText: The service changed this tool. It is blocked until you review the change; runs that use it fail.
services.foreignText: Foreign text from the service: it is shown, but never treated as an instruction.
services.suggested: The service states: {{access}}. This is a hint, not a guarantee.
services.writeBlocked: Tools that change data stay blocked until approval per call is available.
services.argumentsNote: The service sees everything the agent sends it. Connect only services you trust with that data.
services.name: Name
services.urlHint: The address of the MCP endpoint, e.g. https://mcp.example.com/mcp. https only.
services.tokenVault: Stored encrypted and never shown again.
services.tokenSession: No secure key store: the token is kept only until the app closes.
services.tokenKept: Stored – leave empty to keep it
services.loopbackHint: Allows http on this computer (127.0.0.1) for a server you develop yourself.
services.stdioUnavailable: Local servers need the Docker sandbox; it is not available here.

transportHint.http: A remote service at an https address.
transportHint.stdio: A Python MCP server from PyPI, started in an isolated container without network or access to your files.

services.requirementsHint: One PyPI requirement per line. You review and approve the exact versions before the server starts.
services.moduleHint: Started with python -m and this module name.
services.localNote: A local server runs in its own container: no network, no access to your files or keys, limited memory and processes. Servers that need the internet or Node.js cannot be used this way.

oauth.connected: Signed in. Test the connection to load the tools.
oauth.hint: After saving, sign in at the service; Nodestro stores the access encrypted and renews it itself.

stats.title: Operation
stats.limits: Limits: {{parallel}} calls at once, {{perMinute}} calls per minute and service, at most {{servers}} services.

services.resourceToolText: This tool reads only the documents the service lists; other addresses are excluded. If the service changes its list, the tool is blocked until you have reviewed the new list. Contents are external data like every result of a service.
